title: Idgham with ghunnah: merging the noon into ي ن م و: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq 1 to 12 and the noon sakinah rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 4 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Idgham with ghunnah rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 4. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Idgham: merging
points: Idgham letters: ي ر م ل و ن
Two kinds: with and without ghunnah

panels.title: How do I know? Look at the mushaf
points: Tanween written one above the other, slanted

keywords.def: merging the noon into the next letter
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon
the four letters of idgham with ghunnah: ي ن م و

questions.q: Read «حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ» (111:5). How many idgham with ghunnah can you hear?
questions.a: Two: حَبْلٌۭ مِّن (tanween into meem) and مِّن مَّسَدٍ (noon into meem).

questions.q: Which letter is NOT in يَنْمُو?
On the pupil PDF, colour every idgham with ghunnah in Al-Bayyinah 98:2 and Al-Masad 111:1 and 5. Today's rota group reads 97:1 to 5 to the teacher in turn.
Extend: write the word يَنْمُو and colour its four letters.
Stretch: in 97:4 «رَبِّهِم مِّن», which letter is merging, noon or meem?
questions.a: Meem: a meem sakinah merges into the next meem with ghunnah (we learn meem rules in Spring 2).

questions.q: «مِّن مَّسَدٍ»: the noon meets meem (م). How do we read it?
options: Merge into the meem with a two-count hum
questions.a: A) Merge into the meem with a two-count hum. Meem is one of يَنْمُو, so it is idgham with ghunnah. Clear noon is for throat letters; nothing changes into baa.

questions.q: Think again: When two friends hold hands and walk as one, are they still two people? What happens to a noon when it 'holds hands' with the next letter?
questions.a: The noon joins into the next letter and disappears into it, but leaves a two-count hum: idgham with ghunnah.
